canonical_answers.heading: GPU layers (AI & Models)
canonical_answers.answer: Open Settings → AI & Models. Unlock **Show advanced hardware settings**, then adjust **GPU offload layers** (llama.cpp `n_gpu_layers`). More layers = faster but more VRAM; too high can crash. See **Hardware tuning (Internal Engine)** in Library → Qube.

question_patterns: why crash when increasing gpu layers
canonical_answers.heading: GPU offload layers
canonical_answers.answer: **GPU offload layers** move transformer blocks onto your GPU for faster Internal Engine inference. Qube caps the slider from detected VRAM/unified memory and reloads the `.gguf` when you change it. Lower layers if loads crash.

canonical_answers.heading: External Server context
canonical_answers.answer: On **External Server**, Qube does **not** set the host context window — configure it in LM Studio or Ollama. Qube’s **Context limit** only affects client-side **max reply** budgeting. Match the host window to your prompts.

canonical_answers.heading: Temperature
canonical_answers.answer: **Temperature** (default 0.8) controls reply randomness in **Settings → AI & Models → Generation** or the Conversations tools panel. Lower = stricter; higher = more varied. Qube may scale it down slightly on risky turns. See **Generation parameters** in Library → Qube.

canonical_answers.heading: Context limit
canonical_answers.answer: **Context limit** is the shared token pool for prompt + reply (default 32,000). On the Internal Engine it sets n_ctx and reloads the model when changed. Tune it in **Settings → AI & Models → Generation**.

canonical_answers.heading: Max reply tokens
canonical_answers.answer: **Limit maximum reply length** and **Max reply tokens** (Settings → AI & Models → Generation) cap how long each reply can grow. Large prompts or chat history leave less room — see **Generation parameters** in Library → Qube.

canonical_answers.heading: Chat history
canonical_answers.answer: **Chat history** (default 10 messages) controls how many recent session messages Qube sends each turn — in **Settings → AI & Models → Generation** or the Conversations tools panel. This is not Memory Manager long-term recall.

canonical_answers.heading: Search quality (Knowledge)
canonical_answers.answer: Open Settings → Knowledge → **Search quality**. Choose Fast, Balanced, or Power, then tap **Prepare search models** if indexing is not ready.

canonical_answers.heading: Retrieval profile (Knowledge)
canonical_answers.answer: **Retrieval profile** is in **Settings → Knowledge → Retrieval profile**. It is a global orchestration setting for knowledge turns—not Library-only ranking. It controls adapter fan-out, timeouts, cache behavior, and web page fetch depth (Fast = SERP snippets only; Balanced/Thorough fetch pages). Applies to Library, Live Sources, presets, and @internet. Not the same as **Search quality** (embedding presets).

question_patterns: difference between fast balanced and power
canonical_answers.heading: Retrieval profile vs search quality
canonical_answers.answer: **Search quality** (Fast/Balanced/Power) picks embedding/rerank models for **Library indexing**. **Retrieval profile** (Fast/Balanced/Thorough/…) orchestrates **every knowledge turn**—Library, Live Sources, presets, and web—including fetch depth after SERP. Same Fast/Balanced names, different settings under **Settings → Knowledge**.

canonical_answers.heading: Knowledge settings
canonical_answers.answer: Open Settings → Knowledge for library search, embeddings, Live Sources, and presets.

canonical_answers.heading: Hide during fullscreen apps
canonical_answers.answer: Open Settings → Desktop Companion and enable **Hide during fullscreen apps**.

canonical_answers.heading: Recommended setup on Wayland
canonical_answers.answer: On Linux Wayland, open **Settings → Desktop Companion**. Prefer **Use edge dock strip mode (better on Wayland)**; only then try **Try floating overlay on Wayland (experimental)**. Tray and the main window still work if the orb is blocked.

canonical_answers.heading: Try floating overlay on Wayland (experimental)
canonical_answers.answer: **Try floating overlay on Wayland (experimental)** attempts the full orb on Wayland compositors that allow it. If the orb fails, enable **Use edge dock strip mode** instead. See **Desktop Companion on Linux Wayland** in Library → Qube.

question_patterns: how to inspect retrieval for a reply
canonical_answers.heading: INSPECT RETRIEVAL
canonical_answers.answer: On an assistant reply, open **Sources**, then **INSPECT RETRIEVAL** when shown. The inspector shows Summary, Graph, Compare, and Explain tabs for that turn's retrieval and routing.

canonical_answers.heading: Redaction workflow
canonical_answers.answer: Launch with **QUBE_WEB_SEARCH_AUDIT_REDACT=1** and **QUBE_ROUTING_DEBUG_LOG_REDACT_QUERY=1** before enabling web search or routing logs. Clear logs, reproduce once, and share only the tail — see **Settings → Advanced → Diagnostic logs**.

question_patterns: what did qube send off device
canonical_answers.heading: Audit today
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Telemetry → Web discovery** for tier and DDG budgets, **Router Intelligence** for route mix, and **INSPECT RETRIEVAL** on replies for per-turn adapters. Full session egress export is planned for Team.

canonical_answers.heading: Linux install
canonical_answers.answer: Download **AppImage** or **`.deb`** (amd64) from GitHub Releases. Pick **cpu**, **vulkan** (AMD/Intel), or **cuda** (NVIDIA). AppImage: `chmod +x` and run; optional **`install_appimage.sh`** for a menu entry. `.deb`: `sudo apt install ./qube_*.deb` then **`qube`**.

canonical_answers.heading: Privacy tier
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Settings → Knowledge → Web search discovery → Privacy tier**, or use the **Privacy** selector in the Conversations tools panel. Default **Private search** uses DuckDuckGo and Wikipedia only.

question_patterns: how to delete a memory entry
delete a memory in memory manager
canonical_answers.heading: Delete one memory
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Memory Manager**, click **Delete** on a card, and confirm. Deletion is permanent and adds the fact to the negative list so similar facts are not re-extracted.

canonical_answers.heading: Bulk delete
canonical_answers.answer: In **Memory Manager**, filter the list, optionally **Export visible**, then click **Delete all visible** and confirm. Each removed row is added to the negative list.

canonical_answers.heading: Do Not Disturb
canonical_answers.answer: Open Settings → Notifications and enable **Do Not Disturb (critical only)**.

canonical_answers.heading: Audio input device
canonical_answers.answer: Open Settings → Voice & Audio and choose your **Audio input device**.

question_patterns: why is my mic level low
canonical_answers.heading: Microphone level meter (top bar)
canonical_answers.answer: Different mics show different levels on the top-bar meter—that is normal. If yours stays low, raise **input volume** for that mic in your **computer’s sound settings** (and any gain knob on the device), confirm the correct **Audio Input** in Settings → Voice & Audio, and use the **lightbulb hint** to test. You do not need a full bar for voice to work; lower **VAD Threshold** if speech still does not trigger.

canonical_answers.heading: UI language variant
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Settings → General** and choose **British English** or **American English** under **Application language**.

canonical_answers.heading: Chat and library wallpapers
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Settings → Themes → Wallpapers**. Configure **Chat wallpaper** and **Library wallpaper** separately (presets, colours, gradients, or imported images). Press **Apply** to use them in the app.

canonical_answers.heading: Memory automation
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Settings → Memory** for **Enable Memory Enrichment & Reflection**, **Promote well-used memories to preferences**, and **Highlight memories that keep coming back**. Review stored rows in **Memory Manager**.

canonical_answers.heading: Help & guidance
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Settings → Help** for **Open @ Composer Guide**, guided tours, **Open Qube documentation** (Library → Qube), and **Uninstall Qube** instructions. Reset tours via the **Reset Help & Guidance** composer command.

canonical_answers.heading: Uninstall Qube
canonical_answers.answer: See **Uninstall Qube** in Library → Qube or **Settings → Help → Uninstall Qube**. Windows: Settings → Apps or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Qube\unins000.exe`. macOS: **Uninstall Qube.app** on the DMG or Help buttons. Linux `.deb`: **`qube-uninstall`** or **`sudo apt remove qube`**. Delete **`~/.qube`** (or **`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Qube`**) for a full data wipe.

canonical_answers.heading: Update Qube
canonical_answers.answer: Download a newer build from **GitHub Releases** or use **Settings → Help → Software updates → Check for updates**. Install over your existing copy — user data stays in **`~/.qube`** (macOS/Linux) or **`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Qube`** (Windows). **Windows:** run **`Qube-<version>-Setup.exe`** or **`winget upgrade -e --id dagaza.Qube`**. **macOS:** replace **`Qube.app`** from the DMG. **Linux `.deb`:** **`sudo apt install ./qube_….deb`**. **AppImage + install script:** re-run **`install_appimage.sh`** (installs **`~/.local/opt/qube/Qube.AppImage`**). See **Update Qube** in Library → Qube.

canonical_answers.heading: Advanced JSON & logs
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Settings → Advanced** for the **JSON settings** editor and five subsystem **diagnostic logs** (`qube.log`, `llm_debug.log`, routing, web search, skills). See **Diagnostic logs — Settings → Advanced** for what each records.

canonical_answers.heading: Contact & Feedback
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Settings → Contact & Feedback** and click **Report a bug** or **Request a feature** to open the Qube website in your browser.

canonical_answers.heading: AI Engine & model path
canonical_answers.answer: Open Settings → AI & Models. Choose **Internal Engine** or **External Provider**, then set **Active model** (local `.gguf` path or server preset).

canonical_answers.heading: Library search (Knowledge)
canonical_answers.answer: Open Settings → Knowledge. Enable **Local Knowledge Base** / library search toggles and set **Search quality** before expecting `@[tool:library]` hits.

canonical_answers.heading: Conversations (Chat)
canonical_answers.answer: Click **Conversations** in the left navigation (chat icon) to open the main chat view.

canonical_answers.heading: Top bar route indicators
canonical_answers.answer: On Conversations, **● RAG** (Library), **● WEB** (web search), and **● HYBRID** (**Hybrid Internet Mode** / auto web — not Memory+Library HYBRID route). Memory uses `@[tool:memory]` — no MEMORY dot. See **Cognitive Router — how routing works**.

canonical_answers.heading: Ingest documents
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Library**, select **Main** (or a user folder), then click **+** (**Ingest New Document**). Supported types include `.txt`, `.md`, `.pdf`, and `.epub`. If **+** is grayed out, select **Main**—you may have the read-only **Qube** folder selected.

canonical_answers.heading: Chat with document
canonical_answers.answer: In **Library**, single-click a document to preview it, then click the floating **Chat with document** button and confirm. Qube opens **Conversations** with a new thread and an `@[file:…]` attachment prefilled.

canonical_answers.heading: Memory Manager
canonical_answers.answer: Click **Memory Manager** in the left navigation (memory icon) to browse, edit, flag, and delete stored long-term memories.

canonical_answers.heading: Memory tiers and categories
canonical_answers.answer: In **Memory Manager**, use **All tiers** for structural tiers (**Preferences**, **Knowledge**, **Episodes**, **Context**) and **All categories** for labels such as preference, identity, project, knowledge, context, and episode. Combine with **Search memory text…** or **Flagged only**.

canonical_answers.heading: Download models
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Model Manager**, select a repository, choose a GGUF quantization, and click **Download**. When the file is saved locally, click **Load Model** to run it on the Internal Engine, or set the path under **Settings → AI & Models**.

question_patterns: where do i open model manager
canonical_answers.heading: Load a downloaded model
canonical_answers.answer: In **Model Manager**, pick a repo, select a downloaded `.gguf` in **Download Options**, then click **Load Model**. You can also load from **Conversations** tools panel or **Settings → AI & Models**.

canonical_answers.heading: Advanced Telemetry
canonical_answers.answer: Click **Telemetry** in the left navigation for **Advanced Telemetry**: hardware load, **Pipeline Latency**, **Router Intelligence**, **Sidecar Cognition**, and **Inference stack** cards.

canonical_answers.heading: Pipeline Latency
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Telemetry** and read **Pipeline Latency** → **LLM TTFT** (Time To First Token). The same **TTFT** value also appears on assistant replies in **Conversations** after a turn completes. See **Advanced Telemetry — interpreting the dashboard** for causes and diagnosis.

canonical_answers.heading: Router Intelligence
canonical_answers.answer: **Router Intelligence** summarizes recent turns: route mix (MEMORY/RAG/**HYBRID** Memory+Library/WEB/NONE), **Avg retrieval phase**, tuner weights (read-only), and health flags. **● HYBRID** dot is **Hybrid Internet Mode**, not the same as HYBRID route counts. See **Cognitive Router — how routing works**.

canonical_answers.heading: System Load Timeline GPU
canonical_answers.answer: The **GPU** line is **compute utilization %**, not VRAM free/total. CPU-only inference or an idle GPU can show 0% while a model is loaded. See **Advanced Telemetry — interpreting the dashboard**.

canonical_answers.heading: Diagnose slow replies
canonical_answers.answer: Compare **TTFT** on the message with **Pipeline Latency** and **Avg retrieval phase** in **Telemetry**. High retrieval latency → indexing/RAG; high TTFT with low retrieval → generation/hardware. Use **INSPECT RETRIEVAL** on **Sources** for one turn.

canonical_answers.heading: Log file location
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Settings → Advanced** → **Open logs folder** (or `~/.qube/logs/`). Use **View {log name}** for a 500-line in-app tail with optional live refresh.

canonical_answers.heading: Routing debug log
canonical_answers.answer: Enable **Routing debug log** under **Settings → Advanced**, send a chat message, then **View Routing debug log** (`routing_debug.log`). One JSONL line per turn with route, strategy, and retrieval outcome.

canonical_answers.heading: LLM debug log
canonical_answers.answer: **LLM debug log** (`llm_debug.log`) captures `Qube.NativeLLM.Debug` JSON (completion traces, discourse, validation). The Settings toggle controls **file recording**; heavy native prompt dumps also need `QUBE_LLM_DEBUG=1` at launch.

canonical_answers.heading: Route vocabulary
canonical_answers.answer: Qube picks a pathway each turn: **NONE** (self-knowledge), **MEMORY**, **RAG** (Library), **WEB**, or **HYBRID** (Memory+Library). Pre-router attachments and post-router overrides can change the pick. See **Cognitive Router — how Qube routes a chat turn**.

question_patterns: hybrid internet mode vs hybrid route
canonical_answers.heading: Two HYBRID meanings
canonical_answers.answer: **● HYBRID** + **Hybrid Internet Mode** = auto **web** search per turn. **HYBRID** in **Telemetry → Routes** = **Memory + Library RAG** combined. Same word, different mechanisms — see **Cognitive Router — how routing works**.

question_patterns: web toggle vs hybrid internet mode
when to use hybrid internet mode
canonical_answers.heading: Web vs Hybrid Internet Mode
canonical_answers.answer: **Web** toggle (composer) forces web on **every message in this chat** until off. **Hybrid Internet Mode** (tools panel) lets the router **auto-pick WEB** per turn. **`@[tool:internet]`** is single-message explicit web.

question_patterns: why no sources on rag turn
canonical_answers.heading: No citations after routing
canonical_answers.answer: If relevance gates drop all hits or a retrieval route finds **zero** surviving sources, Qube **downgrades to plain chat** before the prompt — no forced citation mode. Check **Sources** on the reply; use **Routing debug log** or **INSPECT RETRIEVAL** for that turn.

canonical_answers.heading: Set up local models
canonical_answers.answer: Use **Model Manager** to download a `.gguf`, set **AI Engine** to **Internal Engine (native)** in **Settings → AI & Models**, then select the model from **LOCAL LLM** in the Conversations tools panel.

canonical_answers.heading: Import documents
canonical_answers.answer: Open **Library → Main**, click **+** (**Ingest New Document**), then prepare search models under **Settings → Knowledge** if search is not ready.

canonical_answers.heading: @ mentions
canonical_answers.answer: Attach `@[tool:help]` for built-in docs, `@[tool:library]` for your uploads, or pick tools from **Attach (@)**. Only the **first routing attachment** in a message controls routing. See **Settings → Help → Open @ Composer Guide**.

canonical_answers.heading: Import button grayed out
canonical_answers.answer: The **+** button uploads to the selected folder. It is disabled on the read-only **Qube** folder and during an active ingest. Click **Main** (or a folder you created), then **+**. Previewing help docs in **Qube** does not block Import unless the **Qube** folder row is selected.

canonical_answers.heading: Empty Library search
canonical_answers.answer: Confirm files finished ingesting (**Chunks Indexed**), search models are ready under **Settings → Knowledge** (**Prepare search models**), and attach `@[tool:library]` or enable **Local Knowledge Base**.
